scan.summary: This is your state license from the OLCC. It allows Evergreen Botanicals, LLC to grow recreational marijuana, up to 10,000 square feet of mature plant canopy indoors, at 2210 Bailey Hill Road only, from March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is getting the renewal in at least 20 days before it expires and meeting the five conditions printed on it, which cover tracking, worker permits, video surveillance and reporting ownership changes.
scan.freshness_note: This is the current one-year term. It was issued March 3, 2026 and is good until March 2, 2027, about five months from today. You don't need a newer copy until the renewal is approved. The signature line on this copy is blank. The framed copy you display at the premises should be the official one from OLCC.

conditions.title: Operate only at the licensed premises. The license can't be moved to another location or transferred to another person.
conditions.evidence_expected: All licensed activity happens at 2210 Bailey Hill Road. Any move or transfer goes through OLCC first, with the approval kept on file.

conditions.title: Renew every year. OLCC must receive the renewal application and fee at least 20 days before expiration.
conditions.evidence_expected: The renewal submission confirmation and fee receipt from OLCC's online licensing system, dated on or before February 10, 2027.

conditions.title: Track every marijuana item at the premises in the Cannabis Tracking System (CTS).
conditions.evidence_expected: An active CTS account, CTS records and reconciliations that match physical inventory, and CTS user credentials for the staff who enter data.

conditions.title: Every employee who handles marijuana items must hold a current OLCC marijuana worker permit.
conditions.evidence_expected: A roster of everyone who handles marijuana items, with each person's worker permit number and expiration date, plus copies of the permits.

conditions.title: Keep video surveillance that meets OAR 845-025-1450, and keep recordings for at least 90 days.
conditions.evidence_expected: A camera layout or coverage plan, proof the system meets OAR 845-025-1450, logs showing it was checked, and proof that at least 90 days of recordings are stored.

conditions.title: Report any change in ownership, in the premises, or in who has a financial interest in the licensee to OLCC before the change takes effect.
conditions.evidence_expected: Change requests filed with OLCC and approvals received before any ownership, premises or financial-interest change, and a current list of financial-interest holders that matches OLCC's records.

conditions.title: Display the license at the premises where the public can see it.
conditions.evidence_expected: The license posted in a publicly visible spot at the Bailey Hill site. A photo of it posted makes a good record.

scan.confidence_notes: I'm highly confident in what I read. The page is one clean, legible page, and every date, number and condition above is copied word for word from it. The one thing not copied is February 10, 2027, which I got by counting 20 days back from March 2, 2027 (February 2027 has 28 days). Outside sources back up the 20-day rule and the yearly cycle: under OAR 845-025-1190, <cite index="8-1">a licensee must renew the wholesaler license at least 20 days prior to the date the license expires</cite>, and OLCC applies the same rule to producers. <cite index="5-6,5-7">OLCC marijuana licensees are required to renew their licenses annually. Licensees are notified 90 days prior to their license expiration date that it's time for license renewal.</cite> That means you should expect a renewal notice in OLCC's online system around early December 2026. Where I'm less sure: (1) The signature line on this copy is blank, so it may be an unsigned or printed copy rather than the official certificate. (2) I did not check the actual requirements in OAR 845-025-1450 (camera placement, resolution and so on). I only restated the 90-day retention printed on the license. (3) Recent rule changes may add renewal requirements not shown on this license. For example, <cite index="6-7">the proposed amendments implement 2025 SB 907 by requiring notarized consent from the owner of the property where any producer or processor license is located</cite>. I haven't confirmed whether that applies at renewal, so ask OLCC or your counsel before February 2027. (4) The page doesn't say whether the company has employees, so I left that fact as unknown.

OREGON LIQUOR AND CANNABIS COMMISSION
9079 SE McLoughlin Blvd, Portland, Oregon 97222
RECREATIONAL MARIJUANA PRODUCER LICENSE
License number: 020-1004763A8B2
Licensee: Evergreen Botanicals, LLC
Trade name: Evergreen Botanicals
Licensed premises: 2210 Bailey Hill Road, Eugene, Oregon 97405
License type: Producer — Tier II, Indoor
Canopy limit: 10,000 square feet mature plant canopy
Original issue date: March 3, 2022
Current term: March 3, 2026 to March 2, 2027
Expiration date: March 2, 2027
This license is issued under ORS 475C and the rules of the Commission in OAR chapter 845, division 25, and
authorizes the licensee to produce marijuana at the licensed premises named above, subject to those rules and to the
conditions below.
Conditions of this license:
1. The license is valid only for the premises named above and is not transferable to any other location or person.
2. The license must be renewed annually. A renewal application and the renewal fee must be received by the
Commission no later than 20 days before the expiration date. A licensee that has submitted a complete renewal
application before that date may continue to operate until the Commission acts on it.
3. All marijuana items at the premises must be tracked in the Cannabis Tracking System, and every employee who
handles marijuana items must hold a current marijuana worker permit issued by the Commission.
4. Video surveillance meeting OAR 845-025-1450 must be maintained at the premises and recordings kept for at
least 90 days.
5. Any change in ownership, in the premises, or in the persons with a financial interest in the licensee must be
reported to the Commission before it takes effect.
This license must be displayed at the licensed premises where it can be seen by the public.
Issued by the Oregon Liquor and Cannabis Commission
Date of issue for the current term: March 3, 2026
Authorized signature: ____________________ Licensing Director
